instructions: Core the tomatoes and slice them into rounds about 1/4 inch thick. Peel the onion and slice it very thinly. Chop 1/3 cup of the parsley.
Overlap the tomato slices on a large platter and sprinkle them with 3/4 tsp of the salt. Scatter the onion over the top.
Drain the tuna well and break it into big chunks. Pile it in the center of the platter.
Scatter the olives over the salad. Drizzle on the 1/3 cup oil and the 3 tbsp vinegar.
Finish with the pepper, the last 1/4 tsp salt and the parsley.
Serve it right away, or keep it in the fridge for up to 1 day.
method_notes: Cuisine de Geraldine (5.00 from 12 ratings) layers sliced tomato, red onion and canned tuna with olive oil, vinegar and parsley, and salts the tomatoes first. Spain on a Fork's Ensalada de San Isidro supplies the olives and uses sherry-vinegar-and-oil dressing with tuna in olive oil. Neither has 20 ratings, so this is a fallback. Capers from the lead were left out, and the salad needs no cooking.
